name: FIGS, Inc.

profile.description: FIGS, Inc. is a digitally native, direct-to-consumer healthcare apparel and lifestyle brand co-founded by Heather Hasson and Trina Spear. It designs and sells premium scrubwear, lab coats, outerwear, underscrubs and lifestyle apparel for healthcare professionals. FY2025 revenue was $631.1M with net income of $34.3M, and Q2 2026 revenue rose 28.8% YoY to $196.6M with net income of $28.4M [1][4]. Management raised FY2026 guidance to ~20% revenue growth with a 14.8-15.0% adjusted EBITDA margin [2]. The stock trades at $21.31 (near its $22.31 52-week high, up from a $7.21 low) for a ~$3.5B market cap [4].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): FIGS created a branded premium category in historically unbranded healthcare apparel and has extended from core scrubs into lab coats, outerwear, underscrubs, lifestyle and international markets, lifting revenue from $263.1M (2020) to $631.1M (2025) [4]. That is a significant new-category build, though not a transformative pivot. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI efficiency gains were found in company disclosures [1][3]. Market Share (2/2): FIGS is the category creator and leader in premium DTC scrubwear, and Q2 2026 growth of 28.8% to $196.6M shows it is still gaining share in its niche [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation products with dated launches and revenue visibility were disclosed beyond ongoing category and international expansion [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FIGS reports zero R&D expense; product development is design iteration within SG&A [4].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): FIGS' stated purpose of celebrating, empowering and serving healthcare professionals ('Awesome Humans') is specific to its customer and shapes product, brand and community decisions [3]. It has been consistent since founding but is not yet validated through a leadership transition or multi-decade crisis. Community Impact (1/2): The Threads for Threads program donates scrubs to healthcare workers in under-resourced settings and is reported in the company's Impact Report, but no large foundation or dollar commitment was found [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or turnover data was found; a 2022 short-seller report alleged employee mistrust of management [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show zero open-market purchases and 13 insider sales from Q4 2025 through Q3 2026, i.e. net selling; capital return has come via the corporate buyback [4][2].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (10 weight units). D/E of 13.0% scores 1.0, and TTM ROE of 14.4% scores 0.96 at 2x weight [4]. Revenue growth of 28.8% YoY (Q2 2026) and a 19.1% 2020-2025 revenue CAGR ($263.1M to $631.1M) both score 1.0 [4]. Forward P/E of 56.7 (price $21.31 / FY2027 consensus EPS $0.376) scores only 0.08, and TTM net margin of 8.7% scores 0.44 [4]. FMP's reported forward PEG of 0.25 scores 1.0 at 2x weight, but note it reflects the sharp rebound in trailing EPS; consensus EPS growth from FY2026 ($0.366) to FY2028 ($0.403) is only ~5% annually, which would imply a far higher PEG [4]. Weighted 8.43/10 rounds to 8. Liquidity is ample at ~3.4M shares/day (~$72M daily dollar volume).

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): PROTECTED. FIGS sells physical garments that clinicians must wear, so AI cannot substitute the product itself; the moat is brand, fabric technology and a professional community [1][3]. Residual exposure sits in the DTC channel, where AI-driven marketing and personalization by larger apparel players could raise customer acquisition competition, and no analyst commentary flags AI as a material risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue or AI-driven savings disclosed [1].

infinite_game.summary: FIGS has a genuine, customer-specific cause in serving healthcare professionals, and leadership held its premium DTC positioning through the 2023-2024 slowdown, a stance now rewarded by 28.8% Q2 2026 growth [1]. But through Sinek's lens the company is still young: it has not been tested by a leadership succession or an existential pivot, the 2022 short-seller allegations around governance and employee trust were never independently resolved, and its competitive language emphasizes category ownership rather than learning from rivals [3][5].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Serving and honoring healthcare professionals is service-oriented and has shaped brand, product and community strategy since founding [3]. It is partially lived (Threads for Threads, healthcare community programs) but has not yet been validated over decades or through crisis [6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept premium pricing and DTC focus while revenue growth slowed to ~2% in 2024 ($555.6M vs $545.6M in 2023), resisting wholesale discounting; growth re-accelerated to 28.8% by Q2 2026 [1][4]. One clear example, not yet a pattern.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Founder continuity is strong, with Trina Spear as CEO and Heather Hasson moving from co-CEO to Executive Chair in 2022 [3]. However, no tenure or turnover data is available, and Spruce Point's 2022 report alleged employee mistrust of management, which keeps this at adequate rather than high trust [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The DTC premium healthcare apparel model is unchanged since founding; expansion into adjacent categories and international markets has been incremental, and the company has not faced a test requiring reinvention [1].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Messaging centers on FIGS as the category creator differentiated from legacy scrub brands; no evidence of management framing competitors as teachers or sources of improvement [3].

investment_thesis: FIGS has inflected from its 2023-2024 trough into high-growth, profitable expansion: Q2 2026 revenue rose 28.8% to $196.6M and net income reached $28.4M, up from $7.1M a year earlier, while management raised FY2026 guidance to ~20% growth and a 14.8-15.0% adjusted EBITDA margin [1][2][4]. The balance sheet is clean (D/E 13%, current ratio 5.0), TTM free cash flow per share is $0.58, and a 19.1% five-year revenue CAGR scores well against IOWN targets [4]. The core product is physical, giving FIGS solid AI resilience, and the Inspire score of 17 carries no negative attributions.
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and durability. At $21.31 the stock trades at 57x trailing and ~57x FY2027 consensus EPS, after roughly tripling from its $7.21 52-week low, while consensus expects EPS of only $0.366 in 2026 and $0.403 in 2028, implying little further earnings growth [4]. Investing.com's call summary indicates growth decelerating to ~20% in Q3 and ~10% in Q4 2026 (unverified against company materials) [2], TTM net margin of 8.7% remains well below the 20% target, and inventory runs ~195 days [4]. Governance and culture questions raised by Spruce Point in 2022 have faded but were never independently resolved [5].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November) will test whether the raised ~20% FY2026 revenue growth and 14.8-15.0% adjusted EBITDA margin guidance hold as comparisons get tougher [2]
Continued margin expansion: Q2 2026 net income of $28.4M on $196.6M revenue (14.4% margin) versus $7.1M on $152.6M a year earlier shows operating leverage in the DTC model [1][4]
Non-scrub categories and international expansion extend runway beyond the core U.S. scrubwear market, supported by a debt-light balance sheet and $0.58/share TTM free cash flow [1][4]
key_risks: Valuation: ~57x trailing and forward earnings with consensus EPS growth of only ~5% annually from FY2026 to FY2028 leaves the stock exposed to multiple compression if growth slows as guided [4]
Reported deceleration toward ~10% growth in Q4 2026 (per Investing.com call summary) could break the momentum narrative after the stock's near-tripling from its 52-week low [2][4]
Inventory of ~195 days and DTC-only distribution expose FIGS to markdown risk and rising customer acquisition costs if well-capitalized apparel brands push into premium medical apparel [4]
